findings: The sequence reads as pressure caught, flank interruption, ice trip, horn cut and regrouping. Distinct recurring silhouettes survive phone width.
The pressure source is visually absent already at G04, before the horn cut in G05. The planned paired-seam transit is not illustrated, and G05 temporarily loses maintained water contact.
G06 restores the ice contact and broken horn but leaves enemies occupying the exit. The art supports a temporary opening under threat, not completed escape.
Framing remains mostly medium action throughout; the intended wider establishment and release were only partly achieved.

The sequence reads as army threat, pressure against formation, returned joint strike, ice evacuation, bridge collapse and continued protected crossing. Changes in shot size and the tall route view give a useful rhythm.
The giant scale and collective stakes survive phone width, as do the three adult weapon/costume signatures where visible. Quiet finishes make the continuous read less fatiguing.

The ice disappears in W05 and reappears in W06; neither full landing topology nor ended growth is established. The final image still contains crossing adults, water contact and an open gate. It cannot prove completed clearance.
The giant joint recoil remains partial and later injury is not distinctly carried forward. Bridge loss is the strongest lasting visible consequence.

The uninterrupted twelve images communicate opposition, parry, damage, forced movement, cost, grasp, relocation, counterstrike, close bind, anchor kick, pressure against pier and aftermath. Camera distance varies within the same recognizable court.
The quiet surface treatment supports a sustained read, expressive faces and clear weapon silhouettes. Particular gains are the diagonal near miss and ice/force applications in the companion studies.

The duel is not mechanically continuous: Ilyra moves/lifts her anchor too early, a landing becomes lower floor without descent, Riven switches saber hands and reuses the wounded side, damage markers drift, and spectators appear then disappear.

D11 has correctly directed shoulder-to-pier contact and a loaded stance. Root reads the held pin more strongly than the instantaneous collision; independent review credits the contact direction while retaining uncertainty about an impulsive hit.
D12 provides a calm release and retains visible cost, but the mantle hole and left-hand saber are actual inconsistencies, not a demonstrated stable state.
